Raw/reconstruction and original temporal shader exports, rejection/clamping, minimum-resource portability, strongest-occluder AO composition, native core data, WebGL2 compatibility and Auto policy are preserved. Compatibility defaults remain blocking/baseline; SM-601 explicitly selects deferred/aggregated.

## Retained physical measurements

Measured clean renderer/harness source: `b1e87b0a8e07ac2ca3e240dbec8f2a708eaa5275`. GTX 1650 SUPER 4 GB, driver 616.92, Windows 11 build 26200, Chrome 154.0.8037.92, non-fallback NVIDIA/Turing with genuine timestamp queries. | 1 | 1.087873 | 1.056064 | 1.288608 |
| 2 | 1.089021 | 1.056064 | 1.286144 |
| 3 | 1.087123 | 1.056768 | 1.286144 |

Mean of run means **1.088006 ms**, worst p95 **1.288608 ms**. The unchanged working mean guardrail is met. This primary distribution is queue-only. A separate same-source diagnostic measures complete command coverage at **1.069927 ms mean / 1.269472 ms p95**; its queue distribution is separate. No CPU, host or map latency is subtracted.

Native production/frozen equivalence passes at four full-HD snapshots and 63 rejection/lifecycle fixtures with exact four temporal textures and eight counter words. The native four-way comparison explicitly tested the combination: queue means were 2.848099 ms baseline, 1.273551 ms deferred-only, and 1.114569 ms combined. Counter blocking alone regressed queue mean to 3.233311 ms; gains are not assumed additive or attributed wholly to shader arithmetic.

Physical GTAO localization exposed an invalid SM-500 command-query resolve: a one-pass frame placed the second resolve at byte offset 16, while WebGPU requires 256-byte alignment. This invalidated the encoder and produced zero-filled readback, which the physical harness correctly rejected.

The repair uses a bounded aligned command section with matching allocation and decoding, preserves queue-only layout and historical aliases, and strengthens mock and real error-scope validation. It also retains an explicit native GTAO decomposition harness and bounded browser-startup handling. Renderer shaders, quality and rejection semantics are unchanged.

At clean source `0c1c707de426fce89ac5f21386ca99edbe8281be`, three fresh Chrome processes on the GTX 1650 SUPER retained 300 warm-up + 600 measured frames each with no WebGPU errors. Pooled queue span was 3.068 ms mean / 3.959 ms p95; independently measured command span was 1.101 / 1.398 ms. Raw horizon/reconstruction/temporal compute means were 0.214 / 0.185 / 0.698 ms. Explicit map waits and timestamp-map latency remain separate CPU metrics; no subtraction manufactures command time.

Source-separated baseline, failed and complete reports are committed under `benchmarks/webgpu-gtx1650s/campaign-2026-10-02-sm500/`. Failed/partial evidence is preserved and excluded from the complete distribution. Native 1920x1080 attachments/DPR1/Medium6x4, driver616.92, Chrome154.0.8037.92, nonfallback NVIDIA/Turing adapter and independent GPU inventory are retained. Observer overhead is documented.

Validation: 83/83 repository checks; alignment/range and 25 changing-count/ring-reuse regression frames; diagnostic shader/fixture preservation; seven startup/identity tests; three physical hardware processes. Required hosted CI remains pending at creation.

This PR adopts no SM-601 optimization, does not close #36 or unblock SM-602, and preserves historical PR #102. Reconciles SM-501 documentation to its verified #92 merge/#31 closure.

Refs #30, #36

issues.body:
## Scope

Follow-up hardening for #30, motivated by the SM-601 / #36 readback investigation. This change fixes the **measurement semantics**, not renderer quality or shader behavior. It does not adopt PR #104, #105 or #106 and does not close #36.

## Problem

The historical SM-500 `gpuMs` wrapper submits one GPU timestamp marker before an async pass callback and another only after the callback returns. It is a legitimate GPU **queue span**, but if the callback submits work and then awaits readback/host work before returning, GPU-idle time can appear between those markers. That span must not be described as pure shader/command execution time.

## Changes

- Preserve `gpuMs` exactly as a compatibility alias of new `queueSpanGpuMs`.
- Add opt-in `commandGpuMs` through `performanceTimingScope.submit(commandBuffers)`: start marker + supplied work + end marker are placed in the same `GPUQueue.submit()`, and multiple explicit submissions are summed.
- Add separately labelled `hostWaitMs` and SM-500 timestamp `readbackMapLatencyMs`.
- Inject the bounded timing scope into attached FrameGraph pass contexts; no queue monkey-patching.
- Bound command spans per pass/frame and reject escaped scopes after callback completion.
- Keep unsupported/disabled timestamp paths functional with null GPU metrics.
- Add explicit queue-span/command-span summaries while retaining historical `summary.gpuPasses`.
- Update the physical target page so existing `gpuRendererMs` output is explicitly sourced from `queueSpanGpuMs`, with timing semantics and explicit-command-span coverage attached to every new result.
- Add the SM-500 validator and contract to the normal repository gate plus a dedicated workflow and canonical documentation.

## Deterministic evidence before PR

A fake timestamp device exercises a deliberate 9 ms synthetic host gap between two explicitly bracketed GPU submissions totalling about 5 ms. The legacy queue span includes that gap; `commandGpuMs` remains the sum of the explicitly submitted GPU work. Additional tests cover FrameGraph scope injection/detach, explicit host-wait accounting, timestamp-unavailable execution, bounded span counts, escaped-scope rejection, disabled instrumentation and memory accounting.

Local syntax + deterministic SM-500 validator pass. These tests prove instrumentation/accounting semantics only; they are **not** physical GPU performance evidence.

## Compatibility / evidence boundary

No historical dataset is rewritten. No CPU time is subtracted from GPU timestamps. No target threshold changes. `steelmoth-webgpu-performance/v1`, frame schema v1, `gpuMs`, and `summary.gpuPasses` remain available.

Command-span attribution is valid only for command buffers explicitly submitted through the timing scope. Existing passes that do not opt in continue to produce queue-span data only, clearly labelled as such.

Keep this PR draft until dedicated SM-500 CI and inherited Verification are green.

## Scope

Refs #36. Implements the requested GTAO reference-mismatch repair, independently of the performance experiments in PRs #104, #105 and #106 and SM-501 / PR #92. **This PR does not close SM-601 or unblock SM-602.**

## Policy decision

Preserve the deployed WGSL rule: reconstruct only when the four-tap weight sum is strictly greater than `f32(0.000001)`; otherwise use nearest raw visibility with confidence zero. Equality falls back.

The original SM-600 merge / PR #96 introduced the JS `1e-8` and WGSL `1e-6` guards together. The original issue/design documents establish bounded depth-aware reconstruction but do not establish the smaller JS number as product authority. Changing the actual shader would be an unrequested rendering-policy change; this repair instead makes the reference describe existing behavior.

One lexical cutoff now drives both the generated WGSL and the CPU predicate. **Both generated production shaders remain byte-for-byte identical**, including the reconstruction SHA-256 `7ddda64b8e31f11998ce77abb721c4b1e105e468e1e3785e28374eb0c9ef81cd`. Runtime class, options, parameter serialization, formats, sample counts and quality semantics are unchanged.

## Regression proof

- Retain the finite binary16-representable 4x4 witness: old reference visibility `0.5591996312141418`; repaired reference `0.25`, confidence `0`, matching the deployed rule.
- Exercise 64 finite fixtures across four debug modes, extreme depth/normal settings, empty/disabled paths, one-pixel/odd extents, duplicate edge taps and binary16 rounding ties.
- 512 seeded randomized independent CPU comparisons.
- Strict equality/adjacent-f32 boundary tests, plus rejected old-cutoff and non-strict-comparison mutants.
- Seven ordinary fixture sets compare legacy/repaired raw, visibility and confidence byte-for-byte on the same JavaScript runtime.
- The new CPU suite is invoked by the existing `validate_webgpu_gtao.js`, so it is included in the normal repository gate.
- A bounded software-WebGPU suite executes actual production reconstruction and a **test-only** lower-threshold control, separately checks exact branch outcomes and numeric output agreement, and repeats with reused resources. It collects no timing.

The reference still uses JS double-precision weighting; it is not claimed to be a universal bit-exact f32 emulator. Exact supplied-sum branch tests are separated from accumulated-sum arithmetic. See `docs/GTAO_REFERENCE_POLICY.md` and the updated canonical SM-600 document.

## Verification at creation

- Local CPU suite: PASS — 256 fixture/debug configurations, 512 randomized cases, 43,737 tested pixels, seven unchanged ordinary scene sets and two rejected policy mutants.
- Inherited GTAO numerical test: PASS locally, using CPU-only resource-loading isolation because this workspace is a partial source copy. No local GPU/resource execution is claimed.
- JS/inline JS syntax, Python compilation and five invalid runner configurations: PASS.
- Original source copies were verified against Git blob hashes; all ten uploaded blobs match the exact locally checked files.
- Hosted shader execution and complete repository checks: **pending at PR creation**, not inferred from the local tests.

## Acceptance and preserved state

This reference-only patch is independently reviewable/mergeable after its actual software-WGSL and inherited checks pass; it does not need a performance-adoption decision because generated shaders and runtime scheduling are unchanged. Do not close #36, change a performance gate, adopt an optimization, mutate retained evidence or rewrite the experiment branches. PR #106's historical mismatch assertion will need explicit reconciliation only if that study is later rebased; its existing evidence remains intact.

issues.body:
## Scope

Refs #36. Carries out the requested GTAO shader arithmetic/memory audit with executable experiments and negative witnesses. **No production adoption, performance claim, issue closure or SM-602 unblock.** PR #92, PR #104 and PR #105 are not edited, stacked or combined.

All six changed files are additions based on `main` `73b6f1222b47219966130a3b135067ef74d65e39`.

## Audit findings

- Reconstruction repeatedly reads the same four half-resolution samples/normals for neighbouring full-resolution outputs. One 8x8 output workgroup needs a 5x5 half-resolution neighbourhood.
- Raw direction vectors, distances and rounded sample offsets are uniform within a dispatch. The supported direction counts include 5 and 7, and radius/normalPower are continuous bounded controls; preset-only shortcuts cannot ignore those values.
- **Existing CPU/GPU reference discrepancy:** the JS reconstruction oracle uses `1e-8`, while WGSL uses `1e-6`. A finite, binary16-representable 4x4 fixture gives weight sum approximately `4.5055614e-7`, JS visibility `0.55919963` versus GPU-equation nearest-raw fallback `0.25`. Neither threshold is changed here.
- A reproducible f32-evaluation witness shows why a CPU trigonometry lookup can move a rounded sample by a full texel. This is a numerical-model witness, not a claimed GPU observation.
- Blindly substituting a coarse hierarchy minimum for a level-zero point sample changes occlusion; a counterexample is included.
- Source-level arithmetic/texture work and descriptor-derived persistent memory are recorded separately from hardware performance and actual DRAM traffic. The current own-resource estimate at 1080p is approximately 114.70 MiB, excluding shared G-buffer/depth resources and driver overhead.

## Isolated candidates

1. **Raw-shared:** evaluate the same WGSL direction/distance/rounded-offset expressions once per 8x8 workgroup, with 472 bytes of workgroup storage and two uniform barriers. No CPU lookup, reciprocal rewrite, sample-count reduction or traversal change.
2. **Reconstruction-shared:** cache 25 raw samples and decoded normals for an 8x8 output tile, using 800 bytes of workgroup storage and one barrier. Preserve weighting, accumulation order, clamped duplicate edge taps, fallback threshold and both outputs.

The standalone probe compares baseline, each candidate independently, and their combination. It preserves the existing `rgba16float` raw intermediate and `r32float` outputs. Padded/disabled lanes reach barriers before returning.

Under the explicit fully occupied source-work model, raw scalar sin/cos evaluations fall from 6,220,800 to 97,920; reconstruction requested texture-read payload falls from 165,888,000 to 46,137,600 bytes. **These are not compiled instruction counts, DRAM-traffic measurements or speedups.** Shared-memory/barrier costs are additional; sparse and empty scenes can regress.

## Local verification completed

- Complete baseline source verified against Git blob `7960a3e12e8ffaa9922f81899e42d326b9a43606`.
- 122 deterministic configurations; 512 seeded randomized cached/direct CPU reconstruction comparisons; 80,628 exact tile-coordinate checks: PASS.
- Every finite binary16 bit-pattern roundtrip, ties-to-even cases, invalid input and source-drift refusal: PASS.
- CPU fallback-threshold mismatch, LUT rounding-boundary and coarse-hierarchy negative witnesses: reproduced and asserted.
- JavaScript syntax, extracted inline browser-script syntax and Python compilation: PASS.
- Six invalid runner argument configurations: rejected with exit 2.
- All six uploaded Git blobs match the exact locally tested files.

**Real shader A/B execution and inherited repository Verification are pending at PR creation.** Local CPU tests do not claim GPU/API execution. The bounded software-only CI job must compile the actual WGSL and compare all three output textures byte-for-byte across 122 cases, each repeated with reused resources. It separately verifies the fallback witness. Exact A/B equality is never replaced by a CPU-reference tolerance.

## Physical handoff

`docs/SM601_SHADER_ARITHMETIC_MEMORY_AUDIT.md` contains the pass/resource inventory, candidate tradeoffs, rejected shortcuts, explicit evidence boundaries and commands. The optional runner requires `--hardware --benchmark`, records raw/upscale compute-pass timestamps separately, rotates variant order, retains raw samples and source/browser/adapter metadata, and supports three fresh-process runs. It must include dense, sparse and neutral controls; it is not full SM-601 acceptance and no timing branch has been executed on physical hardware here.

Keep this PR draft/unmerged. Any production adoption is a separate measured decision followed by the unchanged full SM-601 moving-scene campaign. No quality/threshold/default changes, no CPU subtraction and no acceptance claims.

## Scope

Refs #36. Implements the requested readback-synchronization investigation as a working opt-in temporal producer adapter, separate from PR #104's counter shader candidate. **Do not close #36 or unblock SM-602. No target performance result is claimed.**

## Confirmed issue

The original `WebGPUGTAOTemporal.update()` awaits diagnostic `mapAsync()` even with `wait:false`; its CPU-side history progress also waits for that mapping. SM-500's enclosing ending timestamp is only submitted once the callback returns, so this queue span can include diagnostic delivery/CPU scheduling idle intervals. The existing approximately 2.88 ms physical result is not a shader-only measurement. The size of any performance benefit remains unknown.

## Implementation

- New `engine/webgpu_gtao_readback.js` reuses the production WGSL, parameter serialization, quality policy, resource registry, history formats and output bindings.
- Explicit `statsMode:'deferred'` plus `wait:false` advances enqueued history without awaiting counters. Default blocking behavior is retained in the new adapter; all existing original callers remain completely unchanged.
- Fixed 1–8 slot staging pool (default 3 × 32 bytes), immutable capacity, explicit skip-new-diagnostic-copy on saturation, and bounded completion retention with counted evictions.
- Per-sample frame/epoch/generation/extent/quality/room/device/backend attribution. Out-of-order maps cannot rewind published diagnostics. Delayed samples are not labeled as current.
- Lifecycle-safe invalidation/cancellation, stale pipeline completion guards, device-loss/reset handling, explicit concurrent-update rejection, mapping-error reporting, and no mapped-buffer reuse.
- Standalone real-WebGPU A/B fixture page and bounded software-only CI job. Optional physical diagnostic runner separately records raw horizon/upscale/temporal command timings, instrumented queue span, CPU callback duration and map latency. It never replaces acceptance timing or subtracts CPU time.

## Compatibility and independence

All six changed files are additions. Original engine code, shaders, quality settings, SM-500 instrumentation, acceptance harnesses, old evidence and backend defaults are untouched. PR #92 remains independent at `672c7097`; PR #104 is not stacked or edited. Main baseline is `73b6f122`.

This adapter is selected only by its standalone study page until a separately reviewed adoption decision. It does not silently enable an unmeasured scheduling change in the game.

## Local verification

- 33 controlled CPU/API-ordering tests: PASS, including 512-frame seeded slow-map stress, out-of-order delivery, saturation, resize, invalidation, device loss/reset, close, failed maps/unmaps/submissions, pending compilation, and blocking compatibility.
- Adapter/test/inline-browser JavaScript syntax: PASS.
- Python compilation: PASS.
- Five invalid runner argument configurations: rejected with exit 2.
- Baseline source copy verified against Git blob `8df297355612a7955baa2ce945e54fac12d8ee0d`.
- All six uploaded Git blob hashes match the exact locally tested files.

Hosted real-WebGPU output comparison and repository verification are **pending**, not claimed by the local tests. No local or physical GPU benchmark was performed.

## Handoff

See `docs/SM601_DEFERRED_READBACK_STUDY.md` for API semantics, explicit telemetry-loss boundaries, verification commands, measurement caveats and physical handoff. After software correctness, compare original blocking vs deferred scheduling on the GTX 1650 SUPER before production adoption; then rerun the unchanged complete SM-601 acceptance workload on exact source.

Keep this PR draft/unmerged pending review and physical adoption evidence. No issue closure, target weakening or default change.

issues.body:
## Issue / task

Refs #36 (SM-601). **Research/test tooling only: this PR must not close #36, unblock SM-602, or claim target performance.** Existing physical evidence remains PR #102. SM-501 / PR #92 is untouched.

## Objective

Use the GPU-unavailable period to identify a concrete, correctness-preserving optimization candidate and prepare reproducible verification/measurement rather than stack speculative production changes.

## Findings

- The production temporal shader performs one global diagnostic atomic per accepted pixel and two per rejected pixel: 2,073,600–4,147,200 updates at 1080p on six shared counters.
- `WebGPUGTAOTemporal.update()` awaits diagnostic `mapAsync()` even with `wait:false`. That flag suppresses queue completion waiting, not the map. This is a separate synchronization candidate, deliberately not changed here.
- Existing SM-601 timing encloses raw GTAO, reconstruction and temporal update together. It does not establish which shader or synchronization boundary dominates the retained approximately 2.88 ms result.

## Changes

- Add a test-only WGSL generator guarded by the exact production shader SHA-256. It aggregates the six diagnostics within each 8×8 workgroup, then flushes exact integer totals. All active pixel/rejection math remains byte-preserved; padded lanes still reach both barriers.
- Add CPU/reference, randomized, invalid-input and source-preservation tests.
- Add an isolated real-WebGPU A/B probe comparing all four output textures byte-for-byte and all eight stats words exactly, including edge extents and repeated resource reuse.
- Add a bounded runner: software correctness by default; physical microbenchmark requires explicit `--hardware --benchmark`. Three fresh-process runs, alternating variant order and raw timestamp samples are supported. Its kernel timing is explicitly NOT the original acceptance queue span.
- Add one bounded software-WebGPU CI job and `docs/SM601_GPU_FREE_PERFORMANCE_STUDY.md` with the cost inventory, evidence limits and physical handoff.

## Production / compatibility invariants

No existing runtime, shader, quality preset, material/ownership format, SM-501 branch, benchmark acceptance harness, performance threshold, backend default or existing evidence file changes. The experimental shader is selected only by the standalone study page; it is not wired into production.

The homogeneous full-HD cases reduce global storage atomic updates by 64×; **this is an operation count, not a shader/frame speedup**. The candidate adds workgroup atomics/barriers and still requires actual measurements.

## Verification performed

- Local production source copy verified against Git blob `8df297355612a7955baa2ce945e54fac12d8ee0d`; same blob at measured source `5d1258032b27af270a925e29379e01bc84acf1d7` and current main.
- Node study suite: PASS — 56 reference fixtures, 512 seeded randomized counter cases, full-HD counts, mutation refusal, extent/reason rejection and pixel-body/ABI preservation.
- JS syntax and Python compilation: PASS.
- Five invalid runner command configurations: correctly rejected with exit 2.
- Local real-browser execution: **UNAVAILABLE, not passed**. Browser navigation was refused with `net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR` before the page ran. No policy bypass attempted.
- Hosted CI, real shader execution, target GPU performance, full repository regression and visual acceptance are **not claimed** by these local results. Check the actual final-head CI results.

## Handoff / stopping conditions

After real WGSL correctness is green, run the documented isolated physical A/B probe on the GTX 1650 SUPER. Adopt the candidate in production only in a separately reviewed patch if evidence supports it, then rerun the unchanged full SM-601 moving-scene acceptance campaign on exact source. Do not infer acceptance from microbenchmark timings, lower quality, remove counters, weaken gates, merge this as accepted renderer work, or touch PR #92.

Remain DRAFT / UNMERGED pending review and software shader-validation evidence. No target-GPU access was used.
